title: Sales summary job
summary: A batch job that reads a CSV file of sales and writes the total per region as JSON or CSV, reporting the rows it could not use.

requirements.title: Sum sales per region
requirements.description: salesjob.summary.summarize(text: str) -> dict reads CSV text whose header names the columns region, product and amount (in any order), and returns {"regions": {<region>: {"count": int, "total": str}}, "total": str, "rows": int, "bad": [{"line": int, "reason": str}]}. Amounts are decimal numbers summed exactly and written with two decimals; rows counts the rows used; the header is line 1.

criteria.then: it returns regions {"north": {"count": 2, "total": "5.50"}, "south": {"count": 1, "total": "1.25"}}, total "6.75", rows 3 and bad []

criteria.given: a CSV text with a row whose amount is not a number, a row whose amount is negative, a row with an empty region and a row with a missing field, among good rows
criteria.then: each of those rows is left out of the totals and listed under bad with its line number and a reason, and the good rows are summed

criteria.given: a CSV text whose header has no amount column, or an empty text

requirements.title: Run the sales job from the command line
requirements.description: python -m salesjob <input.csv> [--format json|csv] reads the file (UTF-8) and prints the summary on stdout: JSON by default, {"regions": ..., "total": ..., "rows": ..., "bad_rows": <count>}; with --format csv, the header region,count,total and one line per region sorted by name. Each bad row is reported on stderr as one line starting with "line <n>:". Exit status: 0 when every row was used, 2 when some rows were bad, 1 when the input cannot be read or has no amount column.

criteria.given: a file of good rows only
criteria.when: python -m salesjob is run with its path
criteria.then: it prints the JSON summary with bad_rows 0 on stdout, nothing on stderr, and exits with status 0

criteria.given: a file with two bad rows among good ones
criteria.when: python -m salesjob is run with its path
criteria.then: it prints the JSON summary of the good rows with bad_rows 2 on stdout, one line per bad row starting with "line <n>:" on stderr, and exits with status 2

criteria.given: a path where no file exists, or a file whose header has no amount column
criteria.when: python -m salesjob is run with it
criteria.then: it prints nothing on stdout, names the path on stderr (and, for the header, the missing amount column) and exits with status 1

criteria.when: python -m salesjob is run with its path and --format csv
criteria.then: it prints the lines "region,count,total", then one line per region sorted by name such as "north,2,5.50", and exits with status 0

quality.target: a file of 100000 rows is summarized in under 2 seconds
0 bad rows are dropped silently: every row left out is reported with its line number

constraints: Python 3.11 or later, standard library only (csv, decimal, json, argparse).
The package is salesjob/ at the project root: salesjob/summary.py defines summarize, salesjob/__main__.py the command line.
Amounts are summed with decimal.Decimal, never with float.
Tests live in tests/ and run with pytest from the project root.
